subject: Locked-room delivery & signature workflow for air-gapped updates

Subject: Locked-room delivery & signature workflow for air-gapped updates

Timothy / Lena —

Thanks again for walking the team through the sealed-site constraints on Friday. Per our conversation, I put together a proposed workflow for deliveries of offline artifacts (images, manifests, and signing blobs) and the on-site verification steps the Aurora ops team will perform. Key goals: make handoffs auditable, preserve atomicity of releases, and provide fallbacks if a signature verification fails.

Top-level flow (summary):
- Redwood produces release bundle (OCI-style image tar + manifest + sha256 signature).
- Signing is performed in our secure signing environment. We publish only the signed digest and a signing-cert bundle to the transport manifest. The signing key never leaves HSM.
- Physical transfer: VeriSign Logistics transports sealed media to Aurora locked-room. FieldOps (Lena) performs physical acceptance and initial checksum.
- On-site verification: Aurora runs a local verification tool (hash and signature check) and then a staged install into an isolated staging cluster.
- Chain-of-custody: FieldOps fills out a three-part custody form and returns a scanned copy to Redwood for audit.

I've attached a manifest template and a draft checklist. Please review and call out any missing steps — particularly around who signs the custody docs and where the copy is stored.

Proposed deadlines: bundle availability 2027-03-24 16:00 UTC; physical pickup window 2027-03-25 to 2027-03-26. If we need a later slipstream, flag it now.

Thanks,
Sean

Sean — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifying questions from Aurora Ops:

1) Signing certs: will we get a chain-of-trust bundle that includes the public key fingerprint and the time-stamped signing-cert, or only the final signed digest? We need the cert chain to match our verification process.

2) If a signature fails verification, do you expect the field team to open a secure line to Redwood for a re-signing/rollback, or should we prepare rollback artifacts? What's the SLT for remediation?

3) Chain-of-custody: our compliance officer requires on-paper signatures from a named Aurora on-site engineer plus the courier rep. The scanned copy must be digitally timestamped and sent to compliance within 2 hours of handoff. Can Redwood host the scanned copies in a restricted S3 bucket?

Also: can you confirm the hash algorithm used (we default to sha256) and whether any compression alters the byte stream before hashing?

-Tim
Timothy Ng
Director, Infrastructure Operations — Aurora Health
+1 (617) 555-0120
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Ng <timothy.ng@aurora-health.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fieldops.io>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:37:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Locked-room delivery & signature workflow for air-gapped updates

Timothy — good questions. Quick answers:

1) Cert bundle: yes. We'll provide the signing-cert chain (PEM bundle) and an attestation file that includes signing timestamps and HSM key id. The bundle will live in the manifest and be hashed into the signed envelope.

2) Remediation: our recommended flow is to attempt local remediation first (we will provide rollback artifacts in the same bundle). If the failure is due to a signing mismatch, FieldOps should contact Redwood via a pre-established escalation channel (encrypted workspace + phone). We will stand up a dedicated on-call pod for the first 72 hours post-delivery with a 2-hour response SLO for critical signature failures.

3) Chain-of-custody: Redwood can host scanned custody docs in a restricted S3 path (read-only to Aurora's compliance IAM role). We'll provision access prior to delivery and confirm retention window (default 7 years, configurable).

Hashing: sha256 on the raw tar stream (no additional compression applied by Redwood). Please avoid client-side recompression which would change the digest.

Action items: Marissa to confirm S3 bucket name and IAM ARNs; Markus to validate the signing-cert export format; Soojin to draft escalation contact card.

Marissa
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference

Sean / Tim — from the courier side: VeriSign can provide tamper-evident metal cases with serialized seals. We will record seal ids on pickup and on handoff. We propose a three-person acceptance protocol at the Aurora site: FieldOps engineer, courier lead, and Aurora compliance witness. We will also provide GPS timestamped photos of handoff location, and manifest printed in triplicate.

Logistics note: pickup ETA windows need to be confirmed by 2027-03-24 09:00 UTC to align with our route planning.

Lena

Folks — technical confirmations from the engineering side:

- Signing artifacts: we'll publish the signature as an openpgp detached signature (ASCII-armored) and also a PKCS7 timestamp token. The PEM chain will include our code-signing cert (issued by Redwood CA) and the intermediate CA cert.
- Verification tooling: attached sample tool (small script) verifies raw tar sha256 and then validates the detached signature against the PEM chain. We will ship the verification binary in both x86_64 and arm64 builds.
- Rollback artifacts: the bundle contains a rollback manifest with explicit steps and an image-tagged rollback image. The local verifier will exit with non-zero on mismatch and print a recommended rollback command.

I'll drop the verifier binary and a short README into the Drive link Marissa has.

-Markus
Senior Release Engineer — Redwood Inference
